title: Spring Boot API Docs & Logging: springdoc-openapi, Logback, JSON Logs and MDC
summary: Quick revision notes on documenting Spring Boot REST APIs with springdoc-openapi and Swagger UI, and on configuring Logback: levels per package, structured JSON output, and MDC trace IDs.

chapters.title: springdoc-openapi and Swagger UI: The Mental Model
points: springdoc-openapi scans Spring MVC/WebFlux controllers at startup and generates an OpenAPI 3 spec; Swagger UI is just a static viewer that renders that spec
Starter dependency: springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui (Boot 3+, WebMVC) or -webflux-ui; the old springdoc-openapi-ui artifact is for Boot 2 and does not work on Boot 3
Defaults: spec JSON at /v3/api-docs (YAML at /v3/api-docs.yaml), UI at /swagger-ui/index.html; no code changes needed for a basic spec
springdoc vs springfox: springdoc supports Boot 3 and OpenAPI 3 and is maintained; springfox targets Swagger 2 and is stalled
Gotcha: Boot 3 with the wrong starter or an old springfox on the classpath gives a blank UI or startup errors; use exactly one docs library

chapters.title: Documenting Endpoints and Schemas
points: Endpoint annotations: @Operation(summary, description) on methods, @ApiResponse(responseCode, description, content) for status codes, @Parameter on params, @Tag(name) on controllers to group them
Schema annotations: @Schema(description, example, requiredMode, accessMode) on DTO classes and fields; Bean Validation (@NotNull, @Size, @Min) is picked up automatically as constraints
Global metadata: declare an @Bean OpenAPI with new OpenAPI().info(new Info().title(...).version(...)) plus components().addSecuritySchemes for a bearer JWT scheme
Example: @Operation(summary = "Get user") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "404", description = "Not found") on GET /users/{id}; @Schema(example = "alice@x.com") on the email field
Gotchas: hide internal endpoints or params with @Hidden; return DTOs not JPA entities or the schema leaks internals; use @RestControllerAdvice error types so error responses are documented

chapters.title: springdoc Configuration and Environment Control
points: Key properties: springdoc.api-docs.path, springdoc.swagger-ui.path, springdoc.swagger-ui.operationsSorter=method, springdoc.swagger-ui.tags-sorter=alpha
Limit scanning with springdoc.packages-to-scan or springdoc.paths-to-match; split into multiple specs with GroupedOpenApi beans (e.g. public vs admin groups)
Disable in production with springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false and springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false, set per profile in application-prod.yml
Secured apps: Spring Security blocks /v3/api-docs/** and /swagger-ui/** unless you permitAll them (or protect them deliberately)
Gotcha: leaving Swagger UI public in production exposes your full API surface; and a custom context-path or proxy prefix needs springdoc.swagger-ui.config-url or server URL set to match

chapters.title: Logback Configuration and Log Levels per Package
points: Spring Boot uses Logback by default via spring-boot-starter-logging; levels in order: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR, and the root default is INFO

Per-package levels in application.yml: logging.level.root=WARN, logging.level.com.myapp.service=DEBUG, logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=DEBUG; the most specific package wins and levels inherit from parent loggers
Custom config goes in logback-spring.xml (not logback.xml) so Spring features like <springProfile> and <springProperty> work; core pieces are <appender>, <logger name level additivity>, <root>
Example: a RollingFileAppender with SizeAndTimeBasedRollingPolicy (fileNamePattern, maxFileSize, maxHistory, totalSizeCap) so logs rotate and cannot fill the disk
Gotchas: additivity=true on a child logger with its own appender duplicates every line (set additivity=false); runtime level changes go through /actuator/loggers/{name} with a POST of configuredLevel

chapters.title: Structured JSON Logs, MDC and Trace IDs
points: Structured logging emits one JSON object per line so ELK, Loki or CloudWatch can filter by field; Boot 3.4+ supports logging.structured.format.console=ecs (or logstash, gcp) with no extra library
Before Boot 3.4, use logstash-logback-encoder with LogstashEncoder in logback-spring.xml, or a JSON layout; log arguments as key-value pairs with StructuredArguments.kv("orderId", id)
MDC is a per-thread map: MDC.put("traceId", id) then reference it in the pattern with %X{traceId}; JSON encoders add all MDC entries as fields automatically
Pattern: a OncePerRequestFilter reads X-Request-Id (or generates a UUID), puts it into MDC, sets the response header, and calls MDC.remove or MDC.clear in a finally block

Gotchas: MDC is ThreadLocal so it is lost on @Async, executors and reactive chains unless you copy it (TaskDecorator or Reactor context propagation); with Micrometer Tracing, Boot auto-populates traceId and spanId in MDC; never log passwords, tokens or PII

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Docs and Logging
points: Dependency and URLs: springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui; /v3/api-docs, /swagger-ui/index.html; prod switch springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false
Annotations: @Tag (controller), @Operation (method), @ApiResponse (status), @Schema (field), @Hidden (exclude), GroupedOpenApi (split specs)
Log levels: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR; set with logging.level.<package>=LEVEL; change live via POST /actuator/loggers/<name>
Config files: logback-spring.xml for profiles and appenders; additivity=false to stop duplicate lines; rolling policy with totalSizeCap
JSON and MDC: logging.structured.format.console=ecs (Boot 3.4+); MDC.put in a filter, %X{traceId} in the pattern, MDC.clear in finally
